sovereign_country.strategic_role: 泛欧数字贸易门户、极速低成本在线设立与新锐EMI银行开户

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No BIT or comprehensive DTAA in force for the Cayman Islands; tax cooperation is governed by TIEAs
UK-Cayman Islands Tax Information Exchange Agreement (2009)
Cayman Islands-United States Tax Information Exchange Agreement (2001)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (as extended to the Cayman Islands)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Cayman Islands: Proceeds of Crime Act (2023 Revision), Anti-Money Laundering Regulations (2023 Revision), Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act 2023, Beneficial Ownership Transparency (Companies) Regulations 2023, Companies Act (2023 Revision), Criminal Justice Act, and the Financial Reporting Authority (FRA) AML/CFT Guidance Notes compliant with FATF standards.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport (each director, shareholder and beneficial owner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority in country of residence (e.g., HM Passport Office)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed commercial bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Personal bank reference letter (each beneficial owner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued outside Cayman Islands

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration Form and corporate structure chart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or licensed corporate services provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if notarized outside Cayman Islands

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against the UN Consolidated List, UK OFSI sanctions list, US OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and Cayman Islands Financial Reporting Authority published measures; enhanced due diligence is automatically applied to PEPs; ongoing transaction monitoring and re-screening are applied per the Cayman Anti-Money Laundering Regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cayman Islands General Registry (CIGR) eServices Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the official legal language; proposed company names must be in English using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin translations are not accepted; the name must be distinguishable from existing names and must not be misleading; an Exempted Company name generally must end in 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is held for 90 days from the date of approval and may be renewed for an additional 90-day period via the registered agent or CIGR eServices before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant or registered agent may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands under the Companies Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible for registered office purposes only if the licensed corporate services provider maintains a physical street address in the Cayman Islands for service of process; no physical employee presence in the Cayman Islands is required for hyper-casual mobile game publishing, subject to confidentiality and negative assurance statements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and availability search fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Companies Act fee schedule
Statutory incorporation fee for exempted company with authorized share capital up to US$50,000
Prevailing market benchmark for first-year registered office service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent / corporate services provider fee (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for first-year company management, nominee director where applicable, and statutory representation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of Memorandum and Articles of Association, share documentation and UBO declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed-fee rate for standard exempted company incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille procurement for foreign public documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary fee plus prevailing apostille charge per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening database access
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML data provider (e.g., Dow Jones, World-Check)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription benchmark for low-to-medium-risk UBO screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulatory administrative fee for BO Transparency Act return filing plus compliance agent processing charge

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2023 Revision), Part XII (Exempted Companies), ss. 175–187; ss. 14, 16 (memorandum and certificate of incorporation); s. 177 (declaration of exempted status); s. 182 (registered office); International Tax Co-operation (Economic Substance) Act (2023 Revision).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, General Registry, Cayman Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation of an Exempted Company, issued upon registration of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a Cayman exempted company may incorporate with a single subscriber share. Standard practice: authorized capital of US$50,000 with US$1 paid up on allotment. No escrow account is required. A registered office in the Cayman Islands at a licensed corporate services provider is mandatory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the allotment and issuance of 1,000,000 common shares, par value US$0.0001 each, to the initial subscriber at par be and is hereby ratified and confirmed. RESOLVED, that the registered office maintained in the Cayman Islands by the licensed corporate services provider be approved and adopted, and the provider is authorized to file all notices required by section 182 of the Companies Act. RESOLVED, that [●] be appointed as Director, [●] as Chief Financial Officer, and [●] as Corporate Secretary, to serve until removed by the Board. RESOLVED, that the officers be authorized to execute all incorporation follow-ups, economic substance filings, and banking/EMI account documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Licensed Corporate Services Provider and KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Registry, Cayman Islands (through a licensed Corporate Service Provider under the Companies Management Act)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute an engagement letter with a Cayman-licensed corporate service provider (CSP). Submit CDD/KYC materials for every beneficial owner; the CSP's AML/CFT compliance officer reviews before any registry filing is initiated. Non-resident promoters must use the CSP as statutory agent; no direct public e-filing is available.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of each ultimate beneficial owner
Corporate chart and entity KYC for intermediate shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSP requests enhanced due diligence, provide a notarized explanation and underlying evidence within 5 business days; unresolved queries defer filing until cleared.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, General Registry, Cayman Islands (name check via MyCayman portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed names for preliminary availability; draft and execute the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association, including authorized share capital, objects clause, class rights, and director indemnities; obtain the registered office provider's consent for the effective date.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Trademark/IP holding chart for gaming brands
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected as misleading or similar, the CSP resubmits the next alternative; if the M&A is queried, file a revision letter incorporating the Registrar's comments; no additional fee for resubmission within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Application Submission and Government Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, General Registry, Cayman Islands (e-filing by licensed CSP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the executed M&A, section 177 declaration of exempted status, registered office consent, and initial director consents. Pay the government registration fee (CI$850; approximately US$1,036) plus courier fees through the CSP's registry account. Select standard or expedited processing.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act of initial directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Requisition for defects: answer within 14 days with an amendment letter and corrected schedule; if the application lapses, re-file within 6 months and the previously paid fee is credited less a handling charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation Issuance and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, General Registry, Cayman Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and assigns the company number; the registered office provider confirms the registered office address by statutory declaration; post-incorporation, obtain certified extracts from the General Registry for bank/EMI opening.
required_dossiers: Company number/code issued by the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a typographical or legal defect, file a rectification application; the Registrar issues a replacement within 5 business days; certified copies can be notarized for KYC purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organization and Governance Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors (records maintained at registered office by licensed CSP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial directors adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution to ratify share allotments, approve the registered office, appoint the Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, approve statutory registers, share certificates and common seal if desired, and authorize opening payment/EMI accounts with UK/EU providers. Board documentation should avoid shifting central management and control to the UK.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer nominee is unavailable, the board passes a substitution resolution and records the change in the Register of Directors/Officers; updated consents are filed in the statutory books.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Economic Substance Notification (ESN) and Annual Filing Program
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the first TIA filing window, submit the Economic Substance Notification (ESN) to declare whether the company conducts a Relevant Activity under the International Tax Co-operation (Economic Substance) Act. For hyper-casual game publishing/licensing, prepare a self-assessment memorandum; if no IP-related Relevant Activity is conducted in the Islands, a 'no relevant activity' notification may be appropriate. Set calendar reminders for annual government fees and returns.
required_dossiers: Board position paper on Relevant Activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Queries from TIA are answered by engagement counsel within 14 days; a late ESN may incur an initial penalty of up to CI$5,000, so file before the deadline or apply for a late-filing waiver where facts support one.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UK Overseas Company Registration for Payment Rails (Conditional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: UK Companies House, Registrar of Companies for England and Wales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the Cayman company establishes a UK establishment, e.g., a payment collection office or physical place of business, register as an Overseas Company using Forms OS1 and OS1S within one month of the trigger. Some UK EMIs or AdMob/AppLovin payout arrangements may require this before onboarding. Obtain a UK establishment number and file annual confirmation statements.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of UK establishment address and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Companies House rejects the forms, correct the validation errors and resubmit within 28 days; if no UK establishment exists, document that analysis and defer UK registration to avoid inadvertent UK tax presence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cayman Islands Trade and Business Licensing Board (not triggered — no local business licence required for an exempted non-resident digital publisher)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No Cayman operating or manufacturing permit required; ISIC 5820 software publishing is a fully remote service activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA required; no regulated industrial installation, no discharge to Cayman waters or airshed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. Digital publishing produces no wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste. Data processing for EU users must comply with Cayman Data Protection Act (2021) and UK GDPR where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to a virtual registered office. If a physical office is later opened, Cayman Islands Fire and Rescue Services certification and occupational occupancy clearance must be obtained by the premises owner or branch operator; the exempted company holds no physical plant requiring civil defense clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC); digital portal: GOV.UK (gov.uk), HMRC online services, Government Gateway; VAT registration via form VAT1 or VAT1B (non-established) and OSS portal for digital services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cayman exempted company with no UK physical presence that supplies digital services (hyper-casual mobile games) to UK consumers must: (1) register for UK VAT immediately upon the first supply (no threshold for non-established taxable persons) using form VAT1B transmitted through the Government Gateway; HMRC issues a 9-digit UK VAT registration number (GB GDNNNNNNNNN) and a VAT online filing account; (2) apply for a UK Economic Operator Registration and Identification (EORI) number only if goods move through UK customs borders (not required for pure intangible digital game downloads); (3) obtain a UK Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) only if UK corporation tax registration is triggered (i.e., central management and control exercised in the UK, or a UK permanent establishment arises); otherwise no UK CT registration is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: UK has no check-the-box election. A foreign-incorporated company is UK tax resident solely if its central management and control (CM&C) is exercised in the UK, and a non-UK resident company is chargeable to UK corporation tax only on profits attributable to a UK permanent establishment (PE); if the Cayman board and strategic decision-making remain offshore, no UK registration arises. Relevant statutory elections/notifications: (1) election for non-resident companies to be treated as UK resident for tax purposes under CTA 2009 s.18(3) (rare, treaty-driven); (2) hybrid mismatch reclassification/notice elections under TIOPA 2010 Part 6 (including the 'multi-lateral' and 'dual inclusion income' elections) to neutralize mismatches if the Cayman entity is treated as transparent by the UK; (3) VAT elections: registration for the Non-Union OSS (One Stop Shop) scheme for B2C digital services, VAT grouping election under VATA 1994 s.43A if a UK establishment exists, and the option to tax (OOT) for land (irrelevant here); (4) UK DPT (Diverted Profits Tax) charging statements and Advance Pricing Agreements can be sought to certify no artificial diversion of UK profits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: UK-established businesses: GBP 90,000 (annual taxable turnover, from 1 April 2024); non-established businesses (Cayman company): GBP 0 - compulsory registration from the first B2C supply of e-services (digital games) to UK consumers under the place of supply rules (VATA 1994 Sch. 4A, Article 58 EU VAT Directive retained as UK law) and the Non-Union OSS scheme; there is no distance-selling or small-seller threshold for non-UK suppliers of digital services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The UK does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls for VAT. Mandatory electronic reporting applies through Making Tax Digital (MTD): VAT-registered businesses with turnover above the GBP 90,000 threshold (or voluntarily registered) must keep digital records and file VAT returns via HMRC-recognised MTD-compatible software using Application Programming Interfaces (API) to HMRC's MTD VAT service; Non-Union OSS returns are filed electronically each calendar quarter through the OSS portal. Customs obligations (if any goods are exported) are discharged electronically via the UK Customs Declaration Service (CDS) with CDS API integration for high-volume declarants. No e-invoicing or fiscal stamping is required for pure digital gaming transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Pure digital services (game downloads, in-app purchases, ad monetization) are outside the scope of UK VAT when supplied to consumers outside the UK, and zero-rated for B2B supplies to overseas businesses subject to the 'place of supply' rules: (1) B2C e-services to non-UK consumers are outside the scope because the place of supply is the customer's country; (2) B2B digital services to a non-UK business are outside the scope subject to receipt of the customer's VAT number and evidence of business status; (3) advertising services (the monetization stream) supplied by the Cayman company to ad networks or advertisers located outside the UK are outside the scope; (4) export of goods (not present in this pure digital model) is zero-rated only with proof of export within 3 months. UK VAT on associated UK costs (hosting, agency fees, legal) can be reclaimed via a UK VAT return or the non-established business (VAT126) process only if the company makes taxable supplies in the UK.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD C88/CDS electronic export declaration), Shipper's Export Declaration, Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (for any physical goods; not applicable to pure digital), Commercial Invoice, Export Packing List, Proof of export (port/airport departure stamps or electronic customs movement records), Inward/Outward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 evidence of foreign consideration

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Cayman Islands operates a fully convertible currency regime with no restrictions on capital or current account transactions. Profits can be freely remitted offshore without regulatory hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds required under Cayman law for digital or service-based exports; voluntary surrender available but not statutory.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited feasibility for offshore digital EMIs due to Cayman regulatory constraints; primarily reliant on traditional correspondent banking with strict AML compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening permitted with proper power of attorney and notarized documents; physical presence not always mandatory for exempted companies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, register of directors, beneficial ownership declaration, and source of funds evidence

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'; verification through KYC and beneficial ownership checks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails primarily via SWIFT MT103 for trade settlements; Commercial LC not commonly used for digital services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Exempted Company Annual Return and Annual Government Fee (Companies Act s. 199)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January each year; newly incorporated entities pay a pro-rated fee within 60 days of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 50% surcharge if settled after 31 January; 100% surcharge if unpaid after 30 June; administrative strike-off for persistent non-payment, with restoration subject to arrears, penalties, and re-registration fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority (TIA) via the DITC online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year (e.g., by 31 December for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CI$500 default penalty for late ESN; continued failure attracts penalties up to CI$10,000 and/or up to 2 years' imprisonment; automatic information exchange with UK and EU tax authorities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register annual confirmation and refresh
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Office / Corporate Services Provider; updated particulars filed with the Registrar's Central Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual KYC refresh aligned with the incorporation anniversary or agent's written request; any share transfer or allotment detail must be updated in the BO register within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal offence for company and officers; fines up to CI$25,000 and default-note issuance for non-response; restrictions can be imposed on share transfers and bank-agent continuance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and corporate secretarial compliance review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and Registered Agent (no external filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Performed within 30 days after the annual fee lodgement (February review window)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government sanction; register deficiencies expose directors to breach-of-duty claims and impair banking, EMI, and corporate service provider continuance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit for non-regulated Cayman exempted companies; audit mandatory only for CIMA-licensed entities, listed issuers, or where Articles/lenders require; UK parent consolidation under Companies Act 2006 s. 479 may compel subsidiary audit if the group exceeds the UK thresholds (turnover > £10.2m, balance sheet > £5.1m)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed Cayman GAAP; IFRS, US GAAP, or FRS 102 commonly adopted; UK group consolidation typically applies IFRS or FRS 101/102; accounting records must be kept at least 5 years (Cayman s. 60) and 6 years (UK HMRC); this pipeline applies the 7-year retention standard

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent issues an annual UBO confirmation requesting directors and shareholders to verify register details; share transfers and allotments must update the BO register within 15 days and be filed with the Central Register; non-responsive companies are flagged default and the agent may resign after notice

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 if exemption applies; 10,000 - 25,000 if group or board mandates an audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% main rate of UK Corporation Tax (Financial Year 2024/25); 19% small profits rate for profits below £50,000 with marginal relief between £50,000–£250,000; a Cayman Exempted Company is liable only on profits attributable to a UK permanent establishment (or as UK resident if central management and control is in the UK).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent Box 10% effective rate on qualifying IP income; Video Games Tax Relief (VGTR) up to 18.9% effective rate on qualifying UK game development expenditure (80% core expenditure uplift); R&D SME/ RDEC relief; 100% Annual Investment Allowance; Cayman-side statutory exemption from all Cayman income/corporation tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: UK CT600 Corporation Tax Return; Company Tax Return; filed electronically via HMRC Government Gateway (mandatory) and corporation tax software; includes mandatory supplementary pages CT600E (loans to participators), CT600I (cross-border), CT600J (avoidance), etc.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (per 12-month accounting period); payments on account quarterly for large companies; corporation tax self-assessment (CTSA).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CT600 due 12 months after the end of the accounting period; final corporation tax payment due 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period; instalment payments for large companies (profits >£1.5m) quarterly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distinctive name, Companies House registration number (if UK-registered branch), UTR (Unique Taxpayer Reference), and accounting period start/end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-UK resident Cayman company must input UK establishment number (if registered) and UTR HMRC issued; note absence of a UK Companies House number if no UK branch registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 (Profit from UK PE / taxable profits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-adjusted trading profit after deducting allowable expenses, capital allowances, and reliefs; apportionment of UK PE profit per OECD profit attribution principles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attributed PE profit computed under UK legislation (CTA 2009 s.19-32, 1288) and OECD authorised OECD approach (AOA) for 2016 onward; use separate accounts or formulaic apportionment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains on UK-situated assets; losses set against gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cayman company chargeable on UK property gains and (since 2019) on all assets of a UK PE; notify HMRC NRCGT return within 60 days of disposal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (Loan relationships / derivative contracts / intangible fixed assets)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Debit/credit from financing arrangements, foreign exchange, derivative contracts, and debits on intangible IP assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure arm’s-length interest on intercompany debt; apply CTA 2009 ss.312-479 for UK PE debt; disallow excess interest under corporate interest restriction (TIOPA 2010 Part 10).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (Non-trading loan relationship deficits and management expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-trading deficits and property business expenses; carry back/carry forward claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-UK companies may claim only if expenses relate to the UK PE; otherwise disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Tax reliefs: Patent Box, R&D, VGTR)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reductions from taxable profits or as tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VGTR available only for qualifying core expenditure incurred in connection with relevant games developed for supply; treaty/PEM rules apply if losses allocated to UK PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: UK group relief claims and trading loss carry-forward/carry-back claims (1-year carry-back limited to £2m; 12-month carry-back for terminal losses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cayman parent/group member can surrender relief only via UK PE; overseas loss relief restricted per CTA 2010 Part 5.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total CT liability after reliefs and credits; amounts of payments on account due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Utilise PAYE/NMW not relevant; claim foreign tax credit relief for upstream Cayman taxes if any (none).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border transactions, transfer pricing adjustments, country-by-country reporting (CbCR) position, hybrid mismatches.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete if Cayman-UK transactions exist (royalties, fees, cost-sharing); UK PE must maintain TP documentation; apply HMRC penalties for defective returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: initial £100 (if within 3 months); £200 after 3 months; additional daily penalties of £10/day (up to 900 days) for up to 6 months; escalated to HMRC-determined penalties after 6 months; late payment interest at Bank of England base rate + 2.5%; also 5% late payment surcharge on unpaid tax due 30 days past due.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: UK domestic law imposes no dividend withholding tax (WHT) on distributions by UK companies or on remittances by a UK branch to its offshore head office (branch profits remittance is not taxable in the UK).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief: The UK–Cayman Islands double taxation arrangement does not exist as a full DTA; only a limited exchange-of-information agreement (TIEA - 2010) with no WHT reduction. If the Cayman company were treated as UK resident or held via a treaty jurisdiction, relief requires Form DT (general) or Form DT-Company, a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority (if any) or from the relevant treaty territory, and advance HMRC clearance via Form AP (non-resident company, CTA 2010 s.1119). For UK PE remittances, no WHT applies under domestic law; treaty application moot.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: UK statutory WHT at 20% on UK-source royalties paid to non-residents (ITA 2007 ss. 903 et seq.); Cayman company (with no DTA full relief) exposed to 20% unless qualifying under UK domestic exceptions (e.g., payments for substantial R&D, software “know-how” exceptions may apply narrowly); interest: UK WHT at 20% on UK-source interest (bank interest exception); quoting treaty rates commonly 0% only with treaty partner; Cayman has no treaty, so 20% statutory rate applies; potential DPT (25%) if arrangements lack substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: UK transfer pricing applies to large enterprises (Companies with more than 250 employees, turnover >£50m, or balance sheet >£43m). Master File required if group turnover >£750m and cross-border intercompany transactions; Local File required under UK CbCR regulations (TIOPA 2010 Schedule 19A); HMRC requires contemporaneous TP records; penalty up to 100% of additional tax liabilities (reasonable care applicable); threshold for UK PE transactions is any controlled transaction with UK tax effect, not a monetary de minimis.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: UK has no formal ‘economic substance’ statute but applies diverted profits tax (DPT) at 25% on contrived arrangements (FA 2015 Part 3); OECD BEPS action 5–13 incorporated; HMRC transaction in OECD guidelines. For Cayman vehicle, Cayman Economic Substance Regime (ESR) applies — a tax-DTA-exempted company must demonstrate core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Cayman for ‘relevant activities’ (including distribution and service centres) unless exempted as pure holding entity; hyper-casual gaming IP royalty income may constitute a ‘holding entity’ or IP holding activity requiring economic substance in Cayman, failing which annual filing with the Cayman General Registry and possible penalties up to CI$10,000 plus strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of UK-source digital advertising revenue from AdMob/AppLovin attributed to a UK permanent establishment; false or dishonest CT600 filings; use of offshore shell arrangements that conceal the office from which the trade’s key functions are performed in London.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possession of UK taxes with intent to evade: fines up to £100,000; unlimited fines in higher courts; imprisonment up to 7 years (TMA 1970 s.106); FA 2007 s.206 civil penalties of up to 100% of tax (or 200% in offshore cases); HMRC offshore “Pilot 2” penalties of up to 200% of UK tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: Directors of a UK-resident Cayman company are personally liable for fraudulent trading (Insolvency Act 1986 s.213); joint and several liability for taxes under CTA 2010 s.1093-1104; national insurance & PAYE debt personal liability; travel bans / conduct orders under CDPA 2015; civil restitution; disqualification orders up to 15 years; in the most serious cases extradition and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Diverted Profits Tax / Tax Abuse of Opaque Offshore Structures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cayman exempted company holds the mobile game IP and books UK ad revenue offshore while UK staff have decision-making power (central management & control), or arrangements lack economic substance designed to avoid a UK PE; failure to file a DPT return within 12 months of the accounting period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DPT at 25% of diverted profits (FA 2015 Part 3); HMRC charging interest, penalties of up to 100% of DPT liability” (FA 2015 s.97); risk of CbCR/hybrid mismatch adjustments; information‑notices requiring documents, and penalties up to £3,000 per notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable under s.116(2) Finance Act 2015 for DPT penalties if knowingly concerned in failure to notify; liability for tax-related transactions invalidated under CTA 2010 s.197; travel document restrictions under CDPA; civil recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm’s-length royalty paid by UK PE to Cayman IP owner; excessive management fees; failure to maintain contemporaneous Master/Local File; failure to sign OECD-compliant documentation upon HMRC request (30 days).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: HMRC transfer pricing adjustment with interest; penalties up to 100% of tax lost (FA 2007 Schedule 24), mitigated to 35-70% for careless, 180-220% for deliberate/offshore cases; potential CbCR ‘country-by-countryreporting’ penalties £3,000 per infraction; DPT double-charge possible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed inaccurate returns face Schedule 24 penalties personally if ‘actively involved’ in error; disqualification under Company Directors Disqualification Act 1986 for up to 15 years; restitution claims in civil courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/Counter-Terrorist Financing and Shell Company Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register with the UK Companies House Persons with Significant Control (PSC) register if UK connects are present; non-identification of ultimate beneficial owner; processing of ad-network payouts through opaque Cayman accounts without appropriate AML-KYC; banking through unregulated EMI without business substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to file PSC: criminal offences (CA 2016 s.50); monetary penalties up to £250,000; civil sanctions from FCA/FCA-authorised EMIs; failure to maintain AML/CTF policies under the Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds Regulations 2017: fines unlimited or imprisonment up to 2 years; HM Treasury asset freeze.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/joint operators of unregulated EMIs are personally liable for AMLR 2017 breaches (reg. 94) with unlimited fine and/or 2-year imprisonment; travel bans and asset restraint via Unexplained Wealth Orders (UWOs) and MPC orders; director disqualification; reputational and criminal stigmas.
